thread:
marc: heads up — we got an escalated ticket from Acme: p99 latency spiked from ~300ms to 2.4s around 08:10 UTC after last night's runtime deploy. They attached traces and said API errors are low but tail latency unbearable.
anya: ack. can you paste the span IDs or traces? i'll start digging into dashboards.
support-bot: Customer ticket #C-8142 created by @acme_corp. Customer impact: user-facing latency. SLA: 99.9% p99 target.
marc: pasted two trace ids: 8a7f3b and 8a7f3c (they look like large decoder steps stuck at kvcache flush).
samir: jumping in. quick check: our global p99 graph shows spike at 08:09 but regional dashboards show small blips. looks like aggregated rollup in datadog/metrics layer double-counted some buckets. :thinking_face:
ella: ugh, is this the same histogram-bucket alignment bug we saw last month?
marc: possibly related. the customer's SDK uses long sequences sometimes — that can skew histogram buckets, but the discrepancy between service-level p99 and region-level suggests aggregation mismatch.
anya: i pulled the PromQL used by the grafana panel. it's using histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) without grouping by region or instance. if the rollup was done pre-sum with different bucket boundaries, that will break quantiles.
samir: exactly. i found two exporters: runtime-exporter v1.2 (buckets: [0.005,0.01,0.025,...]) and legacy-exporter v1.0 (buckets: [0.01,0.02,0.05,...]). both reporting same metric name in the same job, so sum() is mixing mismatched le boundaries.
marc: so the p99 panel at org-level uses that promql and shows a large spike, while region panels apply `by (region)` so only like-for-like buckets get aggregated — explains mismatch.
ella: timeline: deploy at 07:58 UTC added a canary host still running legacy-exporter. traffic shifted then and at ~08:09 canary got more traffic -> aggregated view exploded.
anya: repro steps for anyone who wants to validate locally:
```
# reproduce locally by simulating two exporters with different le boundaries
# run prometheus with two scrape targets emitting request_duration_seconds_bucket
# target A: buckets [0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1]
# target B: buckets [0.005, 0.01, 0.025, 0.05]
# then run:
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```
said code will give nonsense quantiles when buckets differ.
marc: customer impact: large p99 graph triggered automated paging and Support escalated. they didn't see errors but UX was impacted. we should communicate cause and short-term mitigations.
samir: mitigation options: 1) revert canary to remove legacy-exporter, 2) change global panel to use `histogram_quantile` after `sum by (le, region)` then `sum by (region)` (i.e., don't mix across different bucket families), 3) add temporary alert suppression for aggregated p99 till fixed.
ella: i'm for immediate revert on canary + fix dashboard query. revert is fastest and lowers customer pain.
anya: i'll patch grafana now to use grouping to avoid cross-bucket sums (safe change), and open a rollback PR for the canary.
marc: also need a durable fix: enforce exporter version gate on instance registers, and add CI that validates bucket compatibility for request_duration_seconds metric across all scrape targets.
support-bot: Noted — will update customer with root-cause explanation and steps we are taking. Draft reply: "we identified metric bucket mismatch between exporter versions that caused aggregated p99 to be incorrect; we reverted the canary and updated dashboards; metrics now show normal tail latency. We're also adding CI checks and stricter version gating."
samir: quick PromQL patch i pushed to staging panel (grafana):
```
# old (bad): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
# new (safer): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, region))
# then collapse: sum by (region) (histogram_quantile(...))
```
anya: deployed panel change to prod, re-evaluating graphs. prod org-level p99 dropped back to expected range at 08:30.
ella: i rolled back the canary at 08:22. can confirm legacy-exporter stopped reporting to prod cluster.
marc: did we cause any backfill anomalies? any alert noise we need to clear?
support-bot: Alert #LAT-TailSpike triggered 23 pages during the window; i suppressed the alert for the aggregated panel at 08:35 to avoid noisy repeats.
samir: action items: 1) enforce exporter version in fleet registration (owner: eng-infra/samir) 2) add unit test in metrics-ci to detect bucket incompatibility (owner: eng-sre/anya) 3) update docs about histogram aggregation gotchas (owner: monitoring/ella) 4) customer comms sent (owner: support-bot).
anya: i'll file the metrics-ci PR and link it here. created ticket METRICS-449.
marc: customer update sent at 09:05 UTC, they confirmed improvement and removed escalation. closing ticket after monitoring for 24h.
ella: note for postmortem: this is not a runtime performance regression — it was observability aggregation mismatch. be explicit in the postmortem so customers understand we didn't ship a model/runtime perf regression.
samir: agree. i'll draft the incident note and include the reproducible PromQL snippet and the fix.
marc: thanks everyone. quick win: dashboard change + canary rollback prevented further customer impact. long-term: enforce exporter compatibility. :thumbsup:
monitoring-bot: Automated task created: METRICS-449, assigned to anya, due 2026-01-12.
support-bot: Ticket #C-8142 marked resolved pending 24h monitoring.
